title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let K/Q_p be finite with ring of integers A, uniformizer π, residue field F_q (q = p^f), and let W ⊂ A be the unramified part W(F_q). Let k be a perfect field containing F_q, with Witt vectors W(k).

Dieudonné module and its decomposition. For a Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) group G_0 over k with an A-action, the Dieudonné module M is a module over A⊗_{Z_p}W(k). It splits as M = ⊕_{ν∈Z/f} M_ν, one summand for each embedding of W(F_q) into W(k). Frobenius F is σ-semilinear and sends M_ν to M_{ν+1}.

What the page computes. In the situation of a preceding proposition, Grothendieck computes the cotangent space ω_{G_0} = t^∨_{G_0} ≅ M_ν/πM_ν (written M_ν/π^F M_ν). He identifies it with Ω/pΩ for an invertible module Ω.
- ω carries two k = F_q-vector-space structures. One comes from the action of A/πA. The other is the natural k-structure, transported by σ^ν.
- They coincide exactly when ν = 0. This is the 'strictness' or 'Lie-compatibility' condition: A should act on Lie(G) through the structural map.
- Using the filtration on M⊗_W k = ⊕ M_ν⊗_A k (rank-1 pieces), he identifies the Hodge line as ω_0 = M_0⊗_A k.

Standard object. The standard case is G_0 = G_0(A,π), with ν = 0 and Ω = A. A general Ω is obtained by the Serre tensor construction Ω⊗_A G_0(A). Its Dieudonné module is:
- M = A⊗_{Z_p}W, free of rank 1 over A⊗W;
- F_M = id_A⊗σ + pr_0((π−1)⊗σ).
Here pr_0 is the projection onto the component for the given inclusion W ↪ A. So F is 1⊗σ on every component except component 0, where it is π⊗σ. Hence F^f = π⊗σ^f on each component. This is the Dieudonné module of the reduction of the Lubin–Tate formal A-module: dimension 1, height [K:Q_p].

Next step. He proposes to lift G_0 to a BT group G over A with an A-action such that A acts on t_G (an invertible A-module) in the evident way, i.e. a strict formal A-module. He invokes Lubin–Tate existence and uniqueness; the page ends there.

Purpose. This is part of the crystals / Dieudonné notes of c. 1970: a Dieudonné-theoretic description of p-divisible groups with A-multiplication, used as test examples for the BT/crystal theory.
errors: ω ≅ Ω/pΩ is dimensionally off when A is ramified. ω_{G_0} is 1-dimensional over k, while for Ω invertible over A⊗W the quotient Ω/pΩ has k-dimension e times larger. It should presumably be Ω/πΩ, or a component of it. This is correct only when A is unramified (π = p).

The formula F = id⊗σ + pr_0((π−1)⊗σ) only makes sense if pr_0 is read as projection onto the 0-th summand followed by re-inclusion. 'W ↪ A' must mean W(F_q) ↪ A, while the σ acts on W(k). These are notational slips, not mathematical ones.
Which of F or V carries the π, and whether ω is M/FM or M/VM, depends on the Dieudonné convention. The page is internally consistent with a contravariant convention.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, early (c. 1970) Dieudonné-theoretic treatment of p-divisible groups with A-multiplication. It identifies the strictness condition (ν=0) and writes down the Dieudonné module of the Lubin–Tate group. That anticipates the style of Drinfeld and Rapoport–Zink, but the content itself is standard and well documented in later literature. It is of mild historical interest only.
transcription_corrections: 'puisque où' is likely 'puisque alors' (a word is struck out after it).
The added marginal insertion 'W/pW =' sits above 'k = F_q', i.e. 'sur W/pW = k = F_q'.
In the filtration line the condition reads roughly 'ω_0 tel que ω_0^{(p)} ⊂ (M⊗_W k)^{...} soit M_{...}⊗_A k'; the indices are uncertain from the image.
'Le cas standard est' is likely 'Le cas standard est celui de'; the following G_0 = G_0(A,π) is written on a new line.
'D'après Lubin-Tate,' ends the page; the left margin carries the insertion 'ou/de A sur t_G soit l'action évidente'.
